replacements.text: Strongest feature: Craig isolates that life-permitting initial conditions occupy a delicate range against life-prohibiting alternatives, making their occurrence surprising and supporting design. Principal limitation: Calling the odds incalculable without specifying admissible possibilities or a defensible probability measure leaves the inference vulnerable to reference-class, selection-effect, and unknown-law objections and cannot identify agency. Live burden: Craig must define the comparison space and distribution, address observational selection, and establish design over chance or necessity, while Flew must explain why specified life-permission remains unsurprising if those foundations are supplied. Locked score: The exact 73 reflects logical coherence 74, evidence warrant 61, responsiveness 86, relevance and burden 81, precision and clarity 72, and calibration and charity 59, rewarding relevance while penalizing evidential underspecification and overconfident probabilistic language.

Strongest feature: Flew distinguishes recognized artifacts from organisms produced through unconscious physical forces, providing a counterexample to an inference that complexity alone establishes intelligent design. Principal limitation: Craig’s evidence concerns specified life-permitting cosmic conditions and comparative improbability, not organismal complexity, so evolution only partially contacts the inference, while identifying artifacts as artifacts risks circularity without an independent criterion. Live burden: Flew must show why fine-tuning lacks design significance if probabilistically defensible, while Craig must articulate a noncircular detection standard when no universe is antecedently known to be manufactured. Locked score: The exact 68 reflects logical coherence 70, evidence warrant 66, responsiveness 65, relevance and burden 70, precision and clarity 76, and calibration and charity 63, crediting conceptual clarity while discounting incomplete contact and an uncharitable reconstruction.
